deep.reconstruction:
Authorship: this page is not by Riemann. It is p. 2 of a letter from Richard Dedekind to Heinrich Weber. The next page closes 'Braunschweig, 6 April 1876 ... Ihr getreuer R. Dedekind'. The letter discusses Weber's proof corrections to Riemann's fragment 'Fragmente über die Grenzfälle der elliptischen Modulfunctionen' (Werke, 1st ed. 1876, pp. 427-438; 'S. 435' is cited). Riemann's 'cases' 1-8 are his formulas for the boundary behaviour (the log of eta-type products) of the modular functions as the variable approaches a rational point m/n. The double parentheses ((x)) denote the sawtooth function: x - floor(x) - 1/2 for non-integer x, and 0 for integer x.

(1) Case 3, continued from the previous page. On the previous page Dedekind reduced a sum by moving the factor s/(2n) inside the bracket. Writing ((s/(2n))) in place of s/(2n) lets the summation run over any complete residue system mod 2n. Substituting sigma -> sigma+n, mu*sigma, mu*sigma+n (mu*m ≡ 1) and adding S and S' gives the linear form
S = 2*Sum_{s=1}^{n-1} (-1)^s ( ((m*s/(2n)+1/2)) - ((mu*s/(2n)+1/2)) ).
He now conjectures that in case 3 Riemann intended the same reduction: Riemann wrote ((s/(4n))) but stopped there. Dedekind could not carry the reduction through either, and says restoring the bracket is optional. He is certain that case 3 must read ((5m/(4n)+1/2)) instead of ((5m/(4n))).

(2) Case 4. He approves Weber's changes, which agree with his own computation.

(3) Case 5 (bottom of p. 435). The second factor 1/(2n) must be deleted. The correct formula is
A + 8*Int_0^1 Sum_{t=1}^{2n} alpha^t dx/(1-alpha^t x) * (1/(2n)) * (-1) * Sum_{s=1}^{2n-1} Sum_{sigma=0}^{n-1} ((sigma-(n-1)/2)/n) * alpha^{m s(2 sigma+1)} * alpha^{-t s}.
Implicit (mine): Int_0^1 alpha^t/(1-alpha^t x) dx = -log(1-alpha^t), so this is a finite Fourier (root-of-unity) expansion of a logarithm. The inner coefficient (sigma-(n-1)/2)/n lies in (-1/2, 1/2) and so agrees with a sawtooth value. The sum over s and sigma acts as a discrete Fourier inversion selecting t ≡ m(2 sigma+1) mod 2n.

(4) Proposal to state explicitly which root of unity alpha is in each case:
- case 2: alpha = e^{2 pi i/(4n)}
- case 3: alpha = e^{2 pi i/(8n)}
- case 4: alpha = e^{2 pi i/(4n)}
- case 5: alpha = e^{2 pi i/(2n)}
- case 8: alpha = e^{2 pi i/(4n)}
He wonders why in cases 2, 3, 7 Riemann did not use alpha^2 in place of alpha and combine the terms at half the spacing.

(5) Case 7. Riemann's two congruences t ≡ 2mr and t ≡ 2mr+2n (mod 4n) coincide as sets once r runs over 1..2n-1 rather than 1..n-1. Implicit (mine): r -> r+n maps one to the other when m is odd. Riemann's final result is nevertheless correct.

(6) He has not yet tried to prove that Riemann's formulas agree with formulas expressed through the symbol (m,n), i.e. Dedekind sums. He suggests keeping ((x)) instead of the integer part E and writing everything as sums over arbitrary complete residue systems: 'Es muß doch gehen!'
errors: No mathematical errors are made by the author on this page. He reports errors in Riemann's fragment as printed in proof: case 3 should read ((5m/4n+1/2)); case 5 has a superfluous second factor 1/(2n); case 7's two congruences are redundant though the end result is correct.
Catalogue issue: the folio is filed under Riemann but the page is in Dedekind's hand, from his 1876 letter to H. Weber.

results.what: Corrected case-5 formula expressing the log as a finite Fourier sum over roots of unity alpha^t with sawtooth coefficients
results.modern_name: Finite Fourier expansion of eta-multiplier / Dedekind-sum data; boundary behaviour of log eta at cusps
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (fragment), edited by Dedekind and Weber 1876

results.what: Observation that t ≡ 2mr and t ≡ 2mr+2n (mod 4n) coincide when r runs over 1..2n-1

deep.surprise_reason: This is editorial correspondence by Dedekind (6 April 1876) on the printing of Riemann's known modular-function fragment. The Dedekind-sum material is well documented as Dedekind's elaboration of Riemann. It contains nothing new by Riemann, though it is a nice archival trace of the editing and of the origin of the (m,n) symbol.

checkable.sympy: saw=lambda x: 0 if x==floor(x) else x-floor(x)-Rational(1,2); n,m=7,3; mu=mod_inverse(m,2*n); S=Rational(2,n)*sum((-1)**s*s*saw(Rational(m*s,2*n)+Rational(1,2)) for s in range(1,n)); L=2*sum((-1)**s*(saw(Rational(m*s,2*n)+Rational(1,2))-saw(Rational(mu*s,2*n)+Rational(1,2))) for s in range(1,n)); S-L
checkable.asserts: Linear form of the previous page that Dedekind hopes to imitate in case 3: (2/n)*Sum(-1)^s s((ms/2n+1/2)) = 2*Sum(-1)^s[((ms/2n+1/2)) - ((mu s/2n+1/2))], mu*m ≡ 1 mod 2n (test with m odd coprime to n); expect 0

The coefficients (sigma-(n-1)/2)/n, sigma=0..n-1, lie strictly in (-1/2,1/2), so they equal their sawtooth values

transcription_corrections: The page is in Dedekind's hand (letter to H. Weber, signed on the next page 'Braunschweig, 6 April 1876, R. Dedekind'), not Riemann's.
'in den {+nicht+} Fällen 2, 3, 7': the interlinear 'nicht' is a placement correction. The sense is 'daß Riemann in den Fällen 2, 3, 7 nicht alpha^2 statt alpha eingeführt ... hat'.
'Vielleicht würde sogar[?]' — reading 'sogar' is plausible but uncertain from the image.
In the case-5 formula the coefficient bracket around (sigma-(n-1)/2)/n may be the sawtooth double bracket ((...)) rather than plain parentheses; the values coincide on the summation range.
